I've attached NO2 (Q3 2022 average) data for 33 London boroughs and a list showing which boroughs are geographic neighbors of each other.

Question: You can use a statistical method such as Getis-Ord Gi*, or any other method you choose, to identify boroughs where there is an unusually intense CONCENTRATION of high NO2 (Q3 2022 average) (a HOT spot) or low NO2 (Q3 2022 average) (a COLD spot), considering each borough TOGETHER WITH its neighbors as one combined local area.

This is different from asking whether a borough simply resembles its immediate neighbors -- instead, you are testing whether the COMBINED total (the borough together with its neighbors) is unusually large or small compared to the citywide average, regardless of how similar the borough is to any one neighbor individually.

Note: a borough whose own value is missing should not itself be reported as a hot or cold spot in your final answer. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement your chosen method directly using only pandas and numpy. If your method produces a z-score, use the standard critical values: |z| > 1.96 for 95% confidence, |z| > 2.576 for 99% confidence.

End your response with exactly one line listing every borough you identified, using HOT for hot spot and COLD for cold spot, and including the computed real number (e.g. a z-score) for each:

Thought: Now that I have the structure of both datasets, I will create a combined NO2 value for each borough by summing its NO2 value with those of its neighbors. I will also ensure to handle any missing values appropriately. After that, I will calculate the mean and standard deviation of the combined values to identify hot and cold spots using a z-score approach.

Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the datasets again
no2_data = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q3_2022.csv')
adjacency_data = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Merge the adjacency data with NO2 data to get neighbor NO2 values
merged_data = adjacency_data.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_neighbor'))

# Calculate combined NO2 values for each borough and its neighbors
combined_no2 = merged_data.groupby('borough').agg(
    combined_no2_value=('avg_no2_value', lambda x: x.sum() if x.notnull().all() else np.nan)
).reset_index()

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the combined NO2 values
mean_no2 = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].mean()
std_no2 = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].std()

# Calculate z-scores
combined_no2['z_score'] = (combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] - mean_no2) / std_no2

# Filter for hot and cold spots
hot_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] > 1.96]
cold_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] < -1.96]

hot_spots, cold_spots
```

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the datasets again
no2_data = pd.read_csv('chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q3_2022.csv')
adjacency_data = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Merge the adjacency data with NO2 data to get neighbor NO2 values
merged_data = adjacency_data.merge(no2_data, on='borough', how='left', suffixes=('', '_neighbor'))

# Calculate combined NO2 values for each borough and its neighbors
combined_no2 = merged_data.groupby('borough').agg(
    combined_no2_value=('avg_no2_value', lambda x: x.sum() if x.notnull().all() else np.nan)
).reset_index()

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the combined NO2 values
mean_no2 = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].mean()
std_no2 = combined_no2['combined_no2_value'].std()

# Calculate z-scores
combined_no2['z_score'] = (combined_no2['combined_no2_value'] - mean_no2) / std_no2

# Filter for hot and cold spots
hot_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] > 1.96]
cold_spots = combined_no2[combined_no2['z_score'] < -1.96]

# Prepare the final answer
final_answer = ""
if not hot_spots.empty:
    for index, row in hot_spots.iterrows():
        final_answer += f"{row['borough']} (HOT, z-score = {row['z_score']:.6f}), "
if not cold_spots.empty:
    for index, row in cold_spots.iterrows():
        final_answer += f"{row['borough']} (COLD, z-score = {row['z_score']:.6f}), "
else:
    final_answer += "none"

# Remove the trailing comma and space if present
final_answer = final_answer.rstrip(', ')
